core_note: From the Core logic page. The comparison there comes from two scout reports dated 2026-10-27 that read public docs, repos and papers; they did not test the tools.

extra.label: Second brain
text: A public slice of the owner's private notes wiki, drawn as a map. Only notes on an approved list are copied, and a build step drops any line that names a private term, a local path, an email or a user name.
Planned, not built: daily news items and job notes, added as drafts that go live only on the owner's weekly OK.

extra.label: Areas of interest
text: The topics the owner writes about. Each links to the pages of this site that cover it, and to the wiki notes that sit under it.

extra.label: Agent harnesses
text: A harness is everything around the model: what it reads, what it may do, and who checks it.

extra.label: Context engineering (ICM)
text: One rules file, linked into every agent tool, plus layers and rooms. The routing table says: for this kind of task, go to this folder and read these files first.

extra.label: AI safety
text: Who may do what: seats, the A0 to A3 ladder and the permission matrix. Short hook scripts turn the most important rules into checks.
swarm-referee is a public repo for the Apart Research AI Collusion Sprint 2026. One worker delivered a reviewed pull request to it.

extra.label: Learning
text: Where the ideas come from: ICM, Kun Chen's agent stack and Matt Pocock's skills. And two checks that found the setup wrong, and what the owner did about each.
links: Safety: checks that proved it wrong

extra.label: Content
text: The owner reviews every report and draft as an HTML page, not in a terminal.

extra.label: FirstMate in detail
text: The twelve parts of the harness, the tricks this setup uses on top, and what it borrowed from others. Each part links to its place on the Core logic page.

extra.label: Always-loaded context
text: Every tool reads one short map first, about 1.5k tokens. The supervisor also reads its rules file each session.
extra.gap: The supervisor's rules file is about 11k tokens, loaded before any work.

extra.label: Rules
text: One rules file, plus a written brief for each task. A routing table says which folder to read for which job.

extra.label: Skills
text: Each skill's name and description load every turn. The body loads only when the trigger fits.

extra.label: Memory and decay
text: At the end of a session, a "stow" step files lessons with decay tiers. Agent memory reaches the curated facts only after review.

extra.label: Hooks
text: Scripts the tool must run. They block file writes through the shell, warn on text shaped like a key, and remind the agent to write a session note.

extra.label: Isolation
text: Each worker gets its own disposable git worktree. Each second mate gets its own home folder.
extra.gap: A worktree isolates files only. It does not fence the network or credentials.

extra.label: Orchestrator
text: The owner talks to one supervisor. Workers are full agent sessions in visible windows. A watcher that uses no tokens wakes the supervisor when needed.

extra.label: Review gate
text: A local gate runs review, tests, docs and lint before the branch leaves the machine. Shell tests check the rule files.
On the Core logic page, Claude Code, OpenCode and Pi lack a gate like this; Omnigent and ICM do the job another way.

extra.label: Human approval points
text: Only the owner merges, publishes, sends or spends. A decision is a task held for the owner. Reviews happen on HTML pages.
extra.gap: The approval and spend rules are prose. The model may not follow them. Omnigent writes the same ideas as enforced policy.

extra.label: Self-improvement
text: A tool called backpass reads past transcripts and proposes rule edits. The owner applies each one by hand.
On the Core logic page, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi and Omnigent lack this. Harness-squared has it with no human step; Meta-Harness searches harness code instead.
extra.gap: A proposed edit is argued from past evidence. It is never tested by replaying a task.

extra.label: Sync across machines
text: Links put the one map where five tools look for it. The supervisor's rules reach running sessions through git.
extra.gap: Agent memory does not sync between machines. (Guess: not checked.)

extra.label: Vision and goals
text: A private owner's layer holds current priorities and preferences, on top of the shared base.
On the Core logic page, ICM, Claude Code, OpenCode, Pi, Warp, Omnigent and Harness-squared lack a goals layer.

extra.label: Routing per task
text: The map holds house rules, a "who does what" list, and a routing table. The routing table says: for this kind of task, go to this folder and read these files first.

extra.label: Plain-English check
text: Scouts run a plain-English checker on their report before they say "done". It flags long sentences and vague words. It is one of the owner's two additions on top of upstream Firstmate.

extra.label: Decay tiers
text: /stow (upstream Firstmate) files durable facts into a curated learnings file, with decay tiers. Status on the Memory page: designed, not proven.

extra.label: Live merge checks
text: A guard. A script registers the pull request and its head commit, and arms a merge poll. The state comes from the forge. It does not come from the worker's message. A draft pull request is refused.

extra.label: Never-send list
text: A short list of terms that must never leave the owner's machine. The build step for this page drops any note line that holds one of them, and also any line with a local path, an email or a user name.

extra.label: grill-with-docs
text: A skill that interviews the owner until the intent is written down in their own words. The idea is from Matt Pocock's skills, which get the agent to ask detailed questions about what you are building.

extra.label: Map shell
text: The interactive Skill map and Harness flow map use the map shell from super-board by EricTechPro (MIT).

extra.label: ARMS framework
text: A framework from Jay E (RoboNuggets) that splits an agent workspace into four layers: Applications, Routines, Memory, Skills.

extra.label: Pi ideas
text: Ideas from the Pi coding agent and its packages. The compaction note cites a Pi extension for server-side compaction.

extra.label: Harness tier list
text: Eleven setups marked on the same twelve harness parts. Has it, does it differently, lacks it, or a guess the scout could not confirm.
The counts treat all twelve parts as equal. They show coverage, not quality. From a scout report dated 2026-10-27 that read public docs, repos and papers; the tools were not tested.
